title: Adaptive requantization pipeline and KV-watermarking for low-latency INT8/FP8 serving
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: production INT8/FP8 serving showed occasional latency spikes when long-lived KV caches and mixed-size sequences interacted with quantization metadata. These spikes occur when a hot prefix reuses KV state but downstream requantization happens at the full sequence boundary, causing a rare but visible token-jitter on P50/P95 for small requests. This PR implements two coordinated runtime features: 1) an adaptive per-token requantization pipeline that performs lightweight per-head rescaling only when KV-reuse heuristics indicate cross-batch scale drift, and 2) a KV-watermark mechanism to limit KV cache growth and trigger lightweight recompact/flush operations before kernels fall back to slow paths. Both features are opt-in runtime flags that default on for dedicated and hosted tiers after canary rollout.

What changed (high level):
- New kernel: runtime/quant/fused_dequant_attn_adaptive.cu — a fused dequant + attention path that accepts per-head scale vectors and a token-adaptive mask. Optimized memory layout reduces temporary allocations in the hot loop.
- Requant pipeline: runtime/quant/requant_controller.cc /.h — tracks per-key/value scale statistics, computes lightweight EMA of per-head scales, and emits per-request hints to the fused kernel. The controller falls back to legacy path if variance is high.
- KV-watermark: runtime/kv/kv_watermark.cc /.h — introduces low/ high watermarks for KV length per-shard; when high watermark is reached the shard runs an incremental recompact that preserves hot prefixes while trimming stale entries.
- Scheduler integration: scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc updated to surface KV hint metadata to the batcher so batches with similar KV fingerprints are coalesced, improving KV-cache hit locality.
- Metrics/tracing: observability/metrics/quant_metrics.cc adds per-request flags and histograms for "requant_taken", "kv_recompact_triggered" and distribution for the time spent in the adaptive kernel.
- Docs and flags: doc/runtime/quant.md and CLI flags for canary rollout, watermark thresholds, and controller aggressiveness.

Compatibility: The adaptive path is compatible with existing model formats and quantization metadata. We fall back to legacy dequant+attn kernels under three conditions: (1) requested model lacks per-head scale metadata, (2) controller variance exceeds configured threshold, (3) explicit compatibility flag off.

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel implementation and unit tests
- [x] Controller logic and integration tests
- [x] Scheduler coalescing for KV fingerprints
- [x] Canary rollout plan and migration docs
- [x] Perf benchmarks and guardrails
- [x] Metrics and alerts

Changes are scoped to serving runtime; no API surface changes to customer-facing Redwood API. Rollout: staged canary (5% hosted, select Dedicated pools), followed by incremental ramp to 100% if perf regressions are absent. Rollback is a single-flag flip or re-deploy of previous runtime which immediately disables adaptive controller and watermarking.

Motivation and technical notes:
- The controller computes per-head EMA of dequant multipliers on a per-key basis; when the EMA delta between the cached multiplier and incoming batch > threshold, the controller marks "requant_taken" for the request and emits a compact scale vector.
- The fused kernel applies per-head scale vectors in-register before matmul to avoid extra roundtrip memory writes; for FP8 paths we preserve exponent biasing when re-scaling.
- KV-watermark uses a two-phase background compaction to avoid blocking foreground inference; compaction is incremental and can be throttled by SLO-aware budget.

Benchmarks summary (internal perf lab, T4-like, seq_len distribution skewed to short sequences):
- Baseline (legacy dequant + attn): p50 token latency 6.8ms, p95 13.2ms, throughput 420 tokens/s
- With adaptive requant + watermark (canary config): p50 token latency 5.5ms (-19%), p95 10.8ms (-18%), throughput 485 tokens/s (+15%)
- Memory: average KV shard memory reduced ~8% after watermark compactions; worst-case memory tail improved ~24%.

Observed slight increase in CPU control-plane time (~2%) for the controller bookkeeping.

Risk analysis:
- Incorrect scale estimation could introduce quality regressions; mitigations: extensive evals included, controller defaults conservative EMA alpha and variance gates.
- Compaction during peak load could interfere with SLOs; mitigations: compaction budget and SLO-aware throttling.

Related work: follows design patterns from prior batching improvements (ENG-4327) and kernel vectorization efforts (ENG-3811).

Priya Singh: Would like a signal when controller is frequently falling back; please emit a rate metric for fallbacks.
Aisha Patel: Added 'requant_fallback_rate' metric and alert runbook entry.

ci_checks: perf-bench: regressions flagged on first run -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Performance: Introduces an adaptive requantization pipeline and KV-watermark compaction which together reduce p50 token latency by ~15-20% on INT8/FP8 workloads and improve throughput by ~10-20% in internal benchmarks. Operators: new runtime flags for enabling adaptive requant controller and KV-watermarks; defaults are off for customers not in canary. Backwards compatible: falls back to legacy dequant path when metadata missing or variance exceeds thresholds.
